cases.question:
Is he a fit for this role? Please list the gaps honestly.

Staff Applied AI Engineer, Conversational Platforms (Berlin or Munich, hybrid)

About us
We build the conversational layer behind customer service for regional banks, insurers and utilities across the DACH region and the Middle East. Our platform handles about two million conversations a month in German, English and Arabic, across chat, email and voice. We are a profitable, 140-person company, and the applied AI group you would join has eleven engineers, two researchers and one product manager.

The team
The Applied AI group owns everything between the raw customer message and the final answer: intent routing, retrieval over customer knowledge bases, tool-using agents that read and update records in our clients' systems, answer generation, safety filters, and the evaluation and monitoring that tell us whether any of it works. We ship every week, we review each other's code, and we write short design documents before large changes. We care about measured improvements more than about new frameworks.

What you'll do
- Own the architecture of our agent runtime: how a conversation is routed between specialised agents, how agents call tools, how state and memory are kept across turns, and how failures are recovered without the customer noticing.
- Design and run retrieval for more than 300 client knowledge bases: chunking, hybrid search, reranking, freshness, access control per document, and multilingual queries where the question is in Arabic and the document in English.
- Lead the move from hosted models to a mix of hosted and self-hosted open-weight models. Plan the GPU capacity, choose the serving stack, and set the rollout and rollback process.
- Build the evaluation system: offline test sets per client, regression suites that run on every change, human review queues, and online metrics for answer quality, latency and cost per conversation.
- Work with our security team on prompt-injection defences, PII redaction in logs, and audit trails that our banking clients can inspect.
- Mentor four to six engineers, run design reviews, and help hire for the group.
- Talk directly with client engineering teams when a deployment needs it, in English or Arabic.

Our stack today
Python 3.12, FastAPI, LangGraph and some in-house orchestration code, PostgreSQL with pgvector, OpenSearch, Redis, Kafka, Kubernetes on AWS (EKS), Argo CD, Terraform, GitHub Actions, Grafana and OpenTelemetry. Hosted models from two providers, and a first self-hosted Qwen deployment on vLLM in a test cluster. Our voice channel uses a streaming speech-to-text service and a text-to-speech service from a partner.

How we work
- Small teams with clear ownership. Each engineer is on call one week in seven, with a quiet rotation and a written runbook for every alert.
- Asynchronous by default: written proposals, recorded demos, and few meetings.
- Four weeks of focused work, then one week for clean-up, documentation and learning.
- A yearly learning budget and two conference trips.

What success looks like in your first six months
- The agent runtime has a written design, an owner for each component, and a failure budget that the team tracks every week.
- Retrieval quality is measured per client, with a dashboard that shows recall and answer correctness for the top 50 clients.
- The first self-hosted model serves at least one production client, with a tested rollback plan and a cost comparison against the hosted models.
- Every change to prompts, models or retrieval runs through the regression suite before release, and the suite is trusted enough that nobody bypasses it.

Requirements
- 6+ years of software or machine-learning engineering, with at least 3 years building LLM or NLP systems that serve real users in production.
- Deep experience with multi-agent or tool-using LLM systems, including routing, memory and failure handling.
- Hands-on retrieval engineering: hybrid search, reranking, and measuring retrieval quality.
- Production experience serving open-weight models with vLLM, TGI or a similar engine on GPUs, including capacity planning.
- Strong Python and API design skills; comfort with asynchronous code.
- Experience building evaluation pipelines for LLM applications, including LLM-as-judge methods and human review, and using them to make release decisions.
- Experience with Kubernetes and infrastructure as code (Terraform) for the services you own.
- Clear written English. Arabic is a strong plus because a third of our traffic is in Arabic.

Nice to have
- German at a working level.
- Experience in regulated industries such as banking or insurance.
- Contributions to open-source LLM tooling.
- Experience with speech pipelines (speech-to-text, text-to-speech) for voice agents.

Additional must-haves for this specific role (please read carefully)
- At least 3 years of production experience writing Rust, because our new low-latency inference gateway and tokenizer services are written in Rust and this role will own them.
- Hands-on fine-tuning of open-weight LLMs with LoRA or QLoRA on proprietary data, with results you can describe against a prompt-only baseline.
- Experience managing engineers formally for at least 2 years, including performance reviews and hiring decisions.

Logistics
- Hybrid: three days a week in our Berlin or Munich office. We support relocation to Germany for the selected candidate and their family, including the visa process.
- Interview process: a 30-minute call with the hiring manager, a take-home design exercise (about three hours, paid), a technical deep-dive on your own past work, a system-design interview, and a conversation with two future teammates.
- Start date: within three months of an offer.
- Salary band and equity are shared in the first call.
